The space I want to cherish the most.

Among the book cafes I decided to visit, the first one by far was ‘Blue Door Books.’
It was quite a distance from home, so I had to make up my mind to go there, but I was willing to take a day off.

Because it is a time reservation system, people who have made reservations wait in line in front of the door before entering. When I hear people who like books express their excitement, I can't hide my excitement.

When I enter, I am greeted by two bookstore keepers and a welcome drink. Then, each person wears their nickname around their neck and takes their place one by one.

The place I chose was Harry Potter.
It seems that it is rare to see people who just take pictures and read books here, but I did my best to sit down.
Although this place is a bit difficult to read a book comfortably, it is fun to watch people enjoying reading.

For two hours, the two bookstore keepers play appropriate background music and always refill drinks to ensure there is no shortage.
In dark places like the Harry Potter seat I was sitting in, they put on an extra light, showing great care and attention to detail. (I liked the BGM Flea, so I also subscribed to the Blue Door Books channel on YouTube.)

It is a place where you can spend a rich time with the curation of two bookstore keepers (you can see it on the bookshelf and through QR), many books in a variety of fields, and each fun place.

Next time, I want to come with my book-loving friends and enjoy this space together.

Atmosphere: The place I went to was in a new building, and the biggest attraction of this place was that you could eat privately in your room. There was a large window in the room, but the view of the parking lot, with a lot of waste materials piled up underneath, was very disappointing.

Service: The attitude of the employees (a young male employee, an older woman, and three young female employees) was disappointing as it showed a lack of professionalism and an immature service spirit. It feels like employees come first, not customers first. (See below for details. Number 4 is the highlight, so I wrote it first. The rest are in chronological order.)

4. While we were continuing our conversation while eating dessert, a male employee came in (he had already paid the bill) and asked if we needed anything else. “Can I get you some more water?” He asked, and when I told him to bring me more, his expression instantly became distorted, and he said, 'I'm telling you to leave, but you don't understand.' It felt like my inner thoughts were revealed, which was surprising and unpleasant at the same time. I drank soda during the meal, so the female companion who came with me kept telling me during the meal that I should drink a lot of water for health reasons, but after seeing the male employee's expression, she said she wanted to leave quickly. I wanted to have a good time with my loved one over a good meal, but the staff's attitude towards customers made it a place I never want to come back to.

1. I made a reservation at 5:30 and checked in about 9 minutes beforehand. When I went to the room I was shown to, I saw that all the side dishes had been set in advance, but some of the side dishes were a little dry.

2. The lady was telling me that she would be serving food, but she spilled her stomach from the raw meat. At first, he just laughed and passed it off, but later, when he tried to put the grilled tenderloin on his plate, he spilled it on the table. They brought the tenderloin back with new meat and grilled it, but he went to get the meat while it was still grilling, and in the meantime, the delicious meat got more and more cooked. I think they should have asked another employee to grill the meat or bring it to them, and I felt a lack of professionalism and responsibility to provide the best taste. 3. The young female employee who puts out the fire after eating the meat tries to remove the charcoal. reviews.text:
The tripe restaurant I recently visited, ‘Jongga House,’ is, in a word, greasy. This is a place where you can feel the old-fashioned atmosphere as a sizable Hanok in Insa-dong has been converted into a restaurant. When the number of customers is high, the interior is filled with tripe oil smoke, but it is not so uncomfortable. The signature performance of this restaurant is to grill the food over a fire and make a fire show outside with soju. The older, ‘girl-crushing’ hall servers who take fresh soju out of the refrigerator and pour it down are cool and friendly.

Opened in 1984, this is a long-established restaurant with 41 years of experience. Use beef tripe. Although the rice was not fried for the second round, the fried rice seemed to be more delicious than other places. Among my Facebook friends, there is one person who is a regular at ‘Jongga House.’ Dongseongdongbon, Hangryeolro is the father of a family and is a foodie. When the reporter said that he only ordered roe-gopchang, he said that he had to mix the amounts together and make sure to stir-fry the rice balls. Another person who works at the Rural Development Administration said that fried rice is a “Korean dessert,” and emphasized that fried rice is a must, “whether stewed, steamed, stewed, or grilled, a dessert made by adding a bowl of rice and stir-frying it after the main dish, shaped into a heart, and garnished with seaweed.”

In fact, the rice stir-fried in giblet oil is savory and has a good flavor. In the past, there was a time when they served hardened tripe oil in milk cartons, but these days, no matter how much you look around, it's hard to find a restaurant like that. We live in an era where health is a concern to bring tripe oil home even once in a while. Meals in restaurants renovated from large and small hanoks are romantic in themselves. Even though it is not neat, there is a warmth.

After leaving Bossam Alley in Jongno, I couldn't find a place to make a quick second stop, so I was drawn to this gomtang restaurant with 85 years of tradition. I have long wanted to come to this long-established restaurant that preserves its heritage within the four main gates.

I liked the exterior, which had the feel of a retro motel that you might find in the countryside. Since it was a weekday evening, it was filled with adults who looked like they were at least company managers. There was even a second floor, so I went up and took a seat.

I knew it wasn't a place where you can eat good value for money like other famous restaurants in Seoul, but the prices weren't as bad as I thought. The reason we came here was for the bones, so two men in their 20s ordered one.

The bones referred to in this house are miscellaneous parts of beef that are used to make gomtang (gomtang) and hangover soup (haejangguk) soup and are steamed together. It costs 45,000 won each, but when I actually received it, I thought it would be enough for three people.

Moreover, it didn't end there, and the bowl of beef soup that came with it was truly an alcoholic beverage. It seemed to be a soup with the same base as the hangover soup they sell, but it was quite oily and rich because it contained cow fat.

Once you have prepared the well-cooked kimchi, radish radish kimchi, and the special sauce provided for each bone, it is time to boil the bones. The special sauce was sour and savory, completely eliminating the smell of the three bones.

The meat attached to the bones was elastic enough to be chewy rather than soft, but it was not tough at all. I could feel the rough charm, beef flavor, and savory flavor that was different from pork backbone.

However, since the previously mentioned Nurin smell is quite strong, there may be differences of opinion, but it contains a lot of soju and goes well with beef soup. The beef in the beef stew was well cooked and really sweet.

Even though I ate for an hour and a half, there was still a lot of soup left, so I regretted coming here first and finishing it. My friend packed up the rest, but I kept thinking about it the next day when I woke up suffering from a hangover.

reviews.text:
A restaurant specializing in gomtang (gomtang)
Located a 1-minute walk from Exit 2-1 of Jongno 3-ga Station.
Tail gomtang costs 29,000 won.
​
What is cost-effectiveness?
After deciding between gomtang and tail gomtang, I decided to try tail gomtang!
The soup tastes like meat broth, like galbitang, and the seasoning is just right.
Is it a bit older and richer than galbitang?
There are two pieces of tail and it tastes like galbitang meat?
Surprisingly, there was no strange taste like intestines, which was fortunate.
However, it is a style that has very little flesh, so it is understandable why people talk about its ‘cost-effectiveness’.
The bones cost almost 10,000 won each, but the meatless tail seems to have disappeared as it was boiled.
The soy sauce-based sauce that came with it was delicious.
They serve kimchi and radish radish as side dishes, and radish radish tastes better than kimchi.
Maybe it's because it's cooked well, but it has a good flavor, so it's great when eaten with rice!
Also, if you eat the tail meat dipped in soy sauce and drink the broth,
The taste suddenly feels bland, so it's okay to add a little soy sauce.
​
Store & Tips & Review
The store is divided into the first and second floors, with the first floor being relatively small.
The second floor feels like a drinking table, and it seems to be closed starting late in the evening.
There are also tables for two, so you can eat alone, and in fact, there are quite a few customers who eat alone.
You order at the table and pay at the counter after eating.
On weekday evenings, you can eat with almost no wait.
The entrance has been remodeled and looks clean, but
The interior overall did not feel clean.
The utensils are a bit annoying, but it's okay for a meal.
There are some reviews that say it is unfriendly, but I didn't feel that when I visited in person.
It is open 24 hours a day, so accessibility is good.
If tail gomtang and gomtang have the same soup base, gomtang would be better unless you are a tail fanatic.

This cozy restaurant sits in a quiet alley just off the path connecting Insadong and Ikseon-dong. While it serves familiar Korean dishes, it carries its own unique character and charm.

In other words, the soup is made using neat Korean-style soybean paste. Based on clear soybean paste and small shrimp, the land and sea meet to provide a refreshing yet deep taste in your mouth.

The highlight is its clear, flavorful broth made from traditional Korean soybean paste (doenjang). Blended with small shrimp, it brings together the earthy taste of the land and the savory essence of the sea — clean, balanced, and deeply comforting.

Another dish is barley bibimbap.

display_name: Wolhadong Wolhadong - Korean traditional pork soup Gomtang
address: 1st floor, 16-1 Insadong 8-gil, Jongno-gu, Seoul, South Korea

reviews.author: Lee Il-gong
reviews.text:
This is a pork soup restaurant where the soup is really clear and light.
The clear soup has no odor and is easy on the stomach, making it easy to eat without feeling burdened. The frozen meat also went well with it. The kimchi was especially delicious!👍🏻
Although it was near a tourist attraction, I was more satisfied with the relatively quiet atmosphere.

reviews.author: Minji Kim
reviews.text:
I went to ‘Wolha-dong’, a newly opened clear pork soup restaurant near Anguk Station! The atmosphere is really nice from the moment you walk in due to the quiet Hanok interior, and there are 13 bar tables, making it a very comfortable place to eat alone.
​My companion and I ordered two servings of gomtang, and we were impressed by how clear the soup was and how it didn't have any porky smell. If you add a little bit of special green bean paste to the soft meat, the umami will explode, and if you add red pepper oil in the middle, you can enjoy another spicy charm.
​More than anything, the taste of the rice is truly a work of art when cooked by blending the best rice! Usually when I eat soup, I have leftover rice, but here I just topped it with 100% domestic kimchi and finished the entire bowl in no time. It was a very satisfying meal as I felt comfortable and did not feel bloated after eating it all. Highly recommended as a filling and clean meal near Anguk Station!

reviews.author: Eunhye Park
reviews.text:
Because it was a quiet and neat atmosphere, meal time felt more leisurely 😊
The clear soup of gomtang is really clean.
It's light but has a subtle, deep flavor.
I felt relieved inside.
And the kimchi was really delicious.
It's crunchy and delicious
Since I eat it with gomtang, I keep reaching for it 🤍

reviews.author: Heegyeong Choi
reviews.text: Absolutely highly recommended!!!! The exterior of the store is pretty, and there is music playing at the entrance, so I feel good from the moment I enter. I ate Wolha gomtang and cold water pork. The soup of gomtang is clear but deep. It has a clean, non-irritating taste. Cold-water meat is also thin and soft, so it has a good texture. The food is neat and luxurious. Judging from the fact that they even run a separate fermentation room, it seems like the owner is serious about the taste. There is bar seating so it's comfortable even if you come alone. Please note the break time is 3:00 PM to 5:00 PM.

reviews.author: joonimism
reviews.text: Sponsorship | I enjoyed pork stew and boiled pork at Wolha-dong, which has a hanok atmosphere in an alley in Insa-dong. There was plenty of thinly sliced ​​pork in a clear and clean soup, so it wasn't heavy at all, and it was accompanied by homemade cheonggeunjang (cheonggeunjang) and kimchi and radish radish made from domestic ingredients, so it was a well-rounded and complete meal. There are bar tables, so it's easy to eat alone, and it was a highly satisfying meal that I'd like to come back to again when I want to eat hot soup quietly near Anguk Station.
